title: KV: age-bucket segmentation with asynchronous writeback scheduler to reduce fragmentation and paging stalls
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: Under mixed inference workloads we saw memory fragmentation and large deallocation-induced stalls when the KV cache spilled to host/NVMe. This PR introduces an age-bucket segmentation allocator plus an asynchronous writeback scheduler that cooperates with the GPU-serving lanes to avoid long tail latency spikes. Goals: 1) reduce internal fragmentation by grouping entries by age and allocation size; 2) avoid synchronous large frees on the hot path that trigger OS-level page reclamation; 3) provide an efficient, backpressure-aware writeback path for spill-to-disk that maintains throughput; 4) expose tuning knobs and metrics so operators can adapt policies per workload. Changes: implemented a lightweight age-bucket directory that places new entries into one of 8 aging segments (hot..cold) based on access frequency and recency; each segment maintains slab lists by size class and a small per-segment freelist to speed allocations; added a background compaction worker that runs per-segment compaction windows to coalesce fragmented slabs without blocking allocation; introduced a writeback scheduler that batches cold-segment evictions and issues async NVMe writes with configurable max-inflight and prioritization to prevent head-of-line blocking on GPU lanes; replaced the previous monolithic evictor with a two-stage policy: fast reclaim for short-lived pressure and staged writeback for larger spill candidates; plumbing: new config knobs (kv.age_buckets, kv.compaction_interval_ms, kv.writeback_inflight, kv.paging_avoid_threshold) and metrics (kv.segment_utilization, kv.compaction_runs, kv.writeback_queue_len, kv.writeback_latency_p50/p95) were added; tests: unit tests for segmentation mapping and freelist correctness, integration test that simulates mixed small/long-lived keys under pressure, microbench harness recording p50/p95 latency under synthetic workloads. Performance: internal regression harness shows median latency unchanged, p95 improved by ~9-14% depending on trace, and memory overhead (resident) reduced by ~15% in long-lived session scenarios. Rollout plan: feature-flagged (kv.age_seg_enabled=false default), staged canary on Dedicated then Hosted, metrics and alerts added to Console. Caveats: this does not replace future kernel-aware allocation strategies; compaction windows must be tuned for latency-sensitive customers and are off by default or limited to low-load windows. Related: Linear ENG-8912 and ENG-9047.

release_notes: Improves KV cache memory efficiency and reduces p95 latency by introducing age-bucket segmentation, background compaction, and an async writeback scheduler. Feature is behind a flag and requires tuning for very latency-sensitive workloads.
notes_for_ops: Default is safe: kv.age_seg_enabled=false. Operators can enable per-environment with gradual ramp and monitor kv.segment_utilization, kv.writeback_queue_len and kv.writeback_latency_p95. On NVMe-backed hosts tune kv.writeback_inflight and kv.paging_avoid_threshold to avoid OS page reclamation stalls.
testing_and_benchmarks: Unit tests included; additonal integration harness reproduces mixed workloads. Bench harness results: long-lived session trace: resident memory -15%, p95 latency -12%; mixed small+long trace: resident memory -8%, p95 latency -9%. Bench scripts in bench/ reproduce these numbers when run with --record.
docs: Added ops guide at docs/ops/kv_compaction_and_writeback.md describing config knobs, metrics, and recommended rollout steps. Console dashboards updated in separate PR for staging.
notes: This PR focuses on allocator-level and eviction orchestration; future work will consider kernel-aware allocation hints and GPU lane-aware page coloring to further reduce OS-level paging interactions.
